title.narrative: Ensuring emergency access for critical health services in Lebanon current conflict

description.narrative: As of October 3, 2024, the MoPH reported 11,330 injured and 1,671 deaths resulting from ongoing hostilities. As of the same date, Lebanon has recorded 346,209 internally displaced persons (IDPs) including 142,361 IDPs registered in 711 collective shelters (Source: DRM/LRC) across 747 cadasters nationwide. The hospital sector is overwhelmed with many reporting shorting in staff that have left to safer areas along with increased number of casualties and shifting patients needing other medical care. The Surveillance System for Attacks on Health Care (SSA) has recorded 35 attacks, resulting in 73 deaths and 67 injuries. These attacks have severely affected health infrastructure, with 18 incidents impacting health facilities and 20 affecting medical transport. Additionally, 26 attacks targeted health personnel, and 10 attacks disrupted the supply of critical medical resources. The recent escalation in violence and conflict has further destabilized the healthcare system, hindering access to essential services and exacerbating existing vulnerabilities. Operational and security challenges have led to the closure around ninety-six centers (PHCCs and dispensaries) in several Governorates as per YMCA data. The conflict has significantly affected the mental health and physical well-being of children and families, leading to alarming levels of psychological distress due to displacement, shelling, and air raids and further intensifying already existing conditions. WHO’s objectives are underpinned by the following outputs:1-Enhancing emergency lifesaving trauma support by procuring vital supplies, implementing targeted training programs, and providing essential staff support for frontline hospitals. 2- Ensuring equitable and timely access to primary healthcare services, including the link with community and outreach activities by ensuring NCD medications access and continuum of care to IDPs.
